rows.clean_note: One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 6 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J1's onboarding, walked IN FILIPINO: index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub, phone-390 mobile+touch, as Romeo Beltran with wh_lang=fil, through the chrome-devtools MCP. THIS WALK FOUND MORE IN THE RULER THAN IN THE PAGES, and both halves are worth recording. THE PRODUCT DEFECT, on the page a worker opens most: hive.html threw a Filipino worker's language away three separate ways - it hardcoded window.WH_LANG='en' in an inline script that runs BEFORE utils.js (so it actively suppressed the platform's own locale floor, and localStorage saying 'fil' rendered ZERO Filipino tokens); setLang never PERSISTED the choice, making it the only one of four toggle-bearing pages that neither read nor saved it; and reading the preference is not applying it, so the ~92 static data-i labels needed the swap run once on load or the board would MEASURE better while the person still read 'YOUR OPEN WORK'. The worker's own card was the last holdout: no data-i on either static label, and of its four JS strings only the ERROR path went through _t() - so the one message a Filipino technician was guaranteed to understand was the failure. All fixed and verified live: 0 -> 34 Filipino tokens, the card now reading 'BUKAS MONG TRABAHO / 4 trabahong nakatalaga sa iyo / I-tap para tingnan at i-update ang mga ito sa logbook mo. / Buksan ang Logbook'. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, which was larger: dim X1 failed on ALL SIX Filipino surfaces (index 0%, asset-hub 38%, alert-hub 67%, hive/logbook/pm-scheduler 80%) where the ENGLISH walk of the same pages failed none - because its guidance vocabulary was English-only on a bilingual product. 'Wala pang nakuwentang Weibull fit. Pindutin...' says PRESS; 'Walang tool na tumugma sa paghahanap' is word-for-word 'No tool matched the search', which passes in English via the match term; 'lalabas dito ang score' is 'a score will appear here', which passes via will-appear. Three groups of Filipino twins were added - action verbs, filter/search terms and reassurance phrases - all MEASURED from the 491 _t(en,fil) strings the platform itself ships (Subukan 119, Buksan 13, Tingnan 7, Pindutin 6, Punan 5), never invented. asset-hub X1 now grades 100% in BOTH languages, and this journey went from fourteen sub-100 dims to seven. Every one of the 62 pending Filipino walks would otherwise have banked the same false dead-ends. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | index 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): B3 - "asset-hub: B3 67% - sentences=3 · >20w=0 · passive=0 · grade>8=1". B3's readability grade is Flesch-Kincaid, whose coefficients are fitted to ENGLISH, and it was applied unchanged to Filipino prose. Measured on the platform's OWN parallel corpus (i18n/*.json holds each English string beside its shipped Filipino): across 193 sentence pairs of 8+ words, the Filipino grades HARDER in 180 of them (93%), mean +4.53 grades, median +4.65; syllables-per-word 1.51 EN vs 1.82 FIL; mean grade 8.7 EN vs 13.3 FIL. 64 pairs PASS in English and FAIL in Filipino, only 2 the other way. The clearest case: "Pick the closest match. You can change scope later." grades 2.3, and its faithful, plain translation "Piliin ang pinakamalapit. Puwede mong baguhin ang scope mamaya." grades 14.1 - the same sentence, +11.8 grades, for being Filipino. Tagalog is agglutinative (naitatala, nagpapalago, disiplinang), so its syllables-per-word runs structurally higher and FK's 11.8 syllable term dominates. These findings measured the LANGUAGE, not the copy, and the platform was being penalised for translating well. The ruler is fixed: Filipino prose is now exempt from GRADE, never from length or voice - the same rule this rubric already applies to standards vocabulary. Only findings that rest ENTIRELY on the grade are withdrawn (no long sentence, no passive voice); English B3 findings stand, because FK is valid for English, and every Filipino finding that also carried a >20-word or passive offence stands on that evidence.

J1 ONBOARDING IN FILIPINO on desktop-1280: index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub, wh_lang='fil', normal conditions, present moment, viewport 1280x900 with mobile/touch emulation OFF. index walked SIGNED OUT (the front door), then in through the platform's own wall, then the member surfaces as Rosa dela Cruz of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet. Every survey taken after a navigation with install:true. 540 dims graded. This is the device/language pair of the English desktop walk banked in the same session, and it found what only a Filipino walk could.

THE FRONT DOOR WAS IN ENGLISH FOR A FILIPINO READER, AND THE TRANSLATION WAS SITTING RIGHT THERE. With wh_lang='fil' and html lang='fil', index rendered 50 of its 56 data-i keys in ENGLISH - "What is WorkHive?", "Install WorkHive", "Today at a Glance", "Free Industrial Tools for Every Filipino Worker" - while _ohFIL, the page's own dictionary, held 58 keys with a Filipino string for every one of them ("Ano ang WorkHive?", "I-install ang WorkHive", "Ngayong Araw sa Isang Tingin"). Nothing was missing and nothing was mistranslated. It simply was never applied.

TWO FAULTS, THE SECOND HIDDEN BEHIND THE FIRST.
(1) THE STORED LOCALE WAS NEVER APPLIED AT BOOT. WH_LANG is read from localStorage on load, so _t()-rendered strings came out Filipino - which is exactly why the page LOOKED bilingual in places and why this survived: "Mag-sign In" and "Higit pa" render through _t(), so a glance suggested the swap was working. But setLang(), which is what applies the dictionary to the static [data-i] markup, was only ever called from the EN/FIL toggle's CLICK handler. A reader who chose Filipino on a previous visit came back to an English front door, every time. Same defect hive.html carried and had fixed earlier the same day (it read a hardcoded 'en' rather than the stored value); this is the landing page's half of it, and it went unnoticed because index is the one page nobody signs in to first.
(2) THE SWAP RAN ONCE, OVER A PAGE HALF OF WHICH DID NOT EXIST YET. setLang snapshotted document.querySelectorAll('[data-i]') and translated exactly that set, so markup rendered LATER kept English permanently: the ops-home panel (#ops-home - "Today at a Glance", "Quick Actions"), the account menu (#user-menu - "Sign out", "Deactivate account", "Change Password") and the PWA install button, all of which paint after auth and data resolve. Proven rather than reasoned: calling setLang('fil') a second time from the console, after everything had painted, flipped all five to Filipino immediately.

FIXED, BOTH HALVES, IN index.html. The dictionary application became _ohApplyI18n(root), which can translate any subtree; a MutationObserver (re-entrancy guarded) runs it on nodes added while FIL is active, so late renders no longer need every renderer to remember; and the stored locale is now applied at boot on DOMContentLoaded. _ohEnCap captures a key's English the FIRST time that key is seen rather than only during the initial sweep, so switching back to English restores late markup too.

Filipino: 0 of 56 keys still showing their English capture (from 50), page text grew 252,226 -> 256,271 characters as the longer Filipino strings landed. English round-trip: setLang('en') restores "What is WorkHive?", "Install WorkHive", "Today at a Glance" - including the late-rendered keys, which is the proof the first-seen capture works - and setLang('fil') returns them. An i18n fix that quietly broke English readers would have been a worse defect than the one it fixed.

The post-sign-in redirect did not land on hive.html and the fallback did not fire, so the file called hive.json carried index's dims - the same "SMRP world-class benchmarks" and "bigSizes=[67,36,30,20]" readings, and 256,289 characters against index's 256,271. THE FRONT DOOR WAS IN ENGLISH FOR A FILIPINO READER, AND THE TRANSLATION WAS SITTING RIGHT THERE. With wh_lang='fil' and html lang='fil', index rendered 50 of its 56 data-i keys in ENGLISH - "What is WorkHive?", "Install WorkHive", "Today at a Glance", "Free Industrial Tools for Every Filipino Worker" - while _ohFIL, the page's own dictionary, held 58 keys with a Filipino string for every one of them ("Ano ang WorkHive?", "I-install ang WorkHive", "Ngayong Araw sa Isang Tingin"). Nothing was missing and nothing was mistranslated. It simply was never applied.

TWO FAULTS, THE SECOND HIDDEN BEHIND THE FIRST.
(1) THE STORED LOCALE WAS NEVER APPLIED AT BOOT. WH_LANG is read from localStorage on load, so _t()-rendered strings came out Filipino - which is exactly why the page LOOKED bilingual in places and why this survived: "Mag-sign In" and "Higit pa" render through _t(), so a glance suggested the swap was working. But setLang(), which is what applies the dictionary to the static [data-i] markup, was only ever called from the EN/FIL toggle's CLICK handler. A reader who chose Filipino on a previous visit came back to an English front door, every time. Same defect hive.html carried and had fixed earlier the same day (it read a hardcoded 'en' rather than the stored value); this is the landing page's half of it, and it went unnoticed because index is the one page nobody signs in to first.
(2) THE SWAP RAN ONCE, OVER A PAGE HALF OF WHICH DID NOT EXIST YET. setLang snapshotted document.querySelectorAll('[data-i]') and translated exactly that set, so markup rendered LATER kept English permanently: the ops-home panel (#ops-home - "Today at a Glance", "Quick Actions"), the account menu (#user-menu - "Sign out", "Deactivate account", "Change Password") and the PWA install button, all of which paint after auth and data resolve. THIS WALK WAS RUN TO TEST A HYPOTHESIS, AND THE ANSWER IS THE RESULT. The Filipino desktop walk banked minutes earlier found index.html never applying the stored locale at boot - setLang() ran only from the EN/FIL toggle's click handler, so 50 of 56 data-i keys rendered English for a reader who had chosen Filipino. The obvious worry was that this was the PATTERN rather than one page's bug: if the landing page forgot, how many others did? So this walk checked the swap explicitly on five member surfaces, reading the rendered text of their data-i nodes rather than trusting a dim.

ALL FIVE APPLY FILIPINO AT BOOT. hive "Markahang nabasa lahat / Gumawa ng Hive / Sumali gamit ang Code / Pumunta sa Live Board", logbook "Ang Iyong Repair Logbook / Irehistro ang Asset / Mag-log", skillmatrix "Mag-log ng trabaho sa Logbook / Paano gumagana ang page", achievements "I-log ang unang entry mo / Tuloy lang! / Paglago", community "Kumokonekta... / I-undo / Walang post na tumutugma / Komunidad". Between them they carry 275 data-i nodes (hive 97, community 62, achievements 48, skillmatrix 47, logbook 21) and the dictionary reaches them on load. So the defect was NOT a platform pattern - index was the outlier, and it was the outlier for a understandable reason: it is the one page a reader can arrive at without ever having signed in, so its boot path is the one nobody exercises while testing a logged-in journey. Worth stating plainly, because "we found it on the landing page" and "the platform does not apply the stored locale" are very different claims and only the first is true.

THE SEVEN FINDINGS BANKED are hive's standing trio (G3 0% - 24 controls with 3 primary CTAs; A3 75%; B3 67%) and a B3 on each of the other four. THE POINT OF THIS WALK WAS TO SECOND-SOURCE THE i18n CLOBBER FIX, AND IT DID. The founder-console find was a single page: whI18nApply's re-apply overwrote every [data-i] element, including those the application had since computed, so a finished value reverted to its placeholder. The fix stamps what the swap wrote (data-i-applied) and skips any element that no longer holds it. hive.html carries the same shape - _elseLine computes a pointer sentence into a data-i element - so it is the honest second case. Probed as a sequence on the live element: read immediately, then again 5s later, past the 200ms-debounced re-apply. Both reads are byte-identical ("Naghihintay din ng review mo: 2 na shift briefing sa Alert Hub") and clobbered=false, with 27 elements carrying the stamp on that page. The mechanism that erased founder-console's health verdict is now proven inert on a second page that was never touched to make it so.

The same line also settles the double-pluralisation I introduced and then fixed: it reads "2 na shift briefing", not "2 na shift briefings". Composing each countable phrase whole per language is holding.

THE NINE FINDINGS. B3 is the pattern, not an incident: four of the six pages fail it (analytics 33%, community 67%, shift-brain 67%, hive 67%) on the same axis - sentences above grade 8, 1 to 4 per page, with no long sentences and almost no passive voice. The prose is not rambling, it is polysyllabic, and it is being read here by a fleet supervisor in her second language. analytics is the worst at 33% (30 sentences, 1 above grade 8, 2 passive).

hive G3 0% is the sharpest single number in the walk: 24 controls on the board and 3 of them are primary CTAs. A3 75% names the same thing from the other side (primaryCta=3/2, 10 disclosures, 0 tabs) - a page that asks for three first actions at once asks for none. analytics E3 50% (the freshness chip reads "Kakakalkula lang - Batay sa iyong logbook", a relative stamp with no absolute time behind it) and R3 67% (one card treatment, four silhouettes across three roles: pill/8px/bar/0px) are ordinary rubric findings on a page that otherwise reads 97%.

dayplanner and ph-intelligence read 100% on their first Filipino walk.

ONE NUMBER I DID NOT BANK AS A DEFECT, ON PURPOSE. analytics N1 scored 75% on "label coverage 1/2, data-i=36, 9 stamped". Four dictionary mechanisms, three of them page-local. The count is unproven in either direction until the instrument knows all four; recorded as an open thread, not a finding. An oracle's vocabulary is part of the oracle.

TWO REAL GAPS THE SAME PASS DID FIND, both in the ONE mechanism it models correctly - i18n/pages/<stem>.fil.json is fetched only when a page carries a [data-i^="p_"] key, and two pages carry p_ keys their page dictionary does not define: ai-quality 4 of 6, platform-actions 23 of 24. Three keys total, silently English for a Filipino reader. Small, specific, and mechanically certain.

Measured on the platform's OWN parallel corpus (i18n/*.json holds each English string beside its shipped Filipino): across 193 sentence pairs of 8+ words, the Filipino grades HARDER in 180 of them (93%), mean +4.53 grades, median +4.65; syllables-per-word 1.51 EN vs 1.82 FIL; mean grade 8.7 EN vs 13.3 FIL. 64 pairs PASS in English and FAIL in Filipino, only 2 the other way. The clearest case: "Pick the closest match. You can change scope later." grades 2.3, and its faithful, plain translation "Piliin ang pinakamalapit. Puwede mong baguhin ang scope mamaya." grades 14.1 - the same sentence, +11.8 grades, for being Filipino. Tagalog is agglutinative (naitatala, nagpapalago, disiplinang), so its syllables-per-word runs structurally higher and FK's 11.8 syllable term dominates. These findings measured the LANGUAGE, not the copy, and the platform was being penalised for translating well. The ruler is fixed: Filipino prose is now exempt from GRADE, never from length or voice - the same rule this rubric already applies to standards vocabulary. Only findings that rest ENTIRELY on the grade are withdrawn (no long sentence, no passive voice); English B3 findings stand, because FK is valid for English, and every Filipino finding that also carried a >20-word or passive offence stands on that evidence. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): E3 - "analytics: E3 50% - chip: "Kakakalkula lang · Batay sa iyong logboo"". E3's freshness vocabulary was ENGLISH-ONLY, so a Filipino page that states its freshness plainly was scored as if it had not. Proven on one page in two languages: analytics reads E3 100% in English on "Saved snapshot, computed 6 min ago · Refresh to recompute" and read 50% in Filipino on "Kakakalkula lang", which is the platform's own shipped translation of "Recomputed just now" - the SAME freshness claim, invisible because the pattern only spoke English. Measured across the dictionaries: 44 English strings carry a freshness word, 25 keep it in Filipino by loanword (snapshot, refresh, generate survive translation) and 19 do not, and those 19 were unreadable to this dim. The ruler is fixed with exactly those measured forms - kalkula/kuwenta (the two verbs Filipino uses for compute), binubuo (built), hiniling (on demand), nakalipas (ago), and the na-/nire- prefixed loanwords the English stems miss because the pattern demands the -d participle. Verified on six cases including the negatives: a chip that names only its SOURCE ("Batay sa iyong logbook", "Based on your logbook") still fails in both languages, so the dim keeps its teeth. Retracted here are ONLY the Filipino findings whose quoted chip the corrected vocabulary now accepts - every one of them a chip that was present and did state its freshness. The Filipino "NO source chip" findings are untouched, because a genuinely missing chip is a real defect in any language, and every English E3 finding stands, because the pattern was always valid for English. This is the fourth English-only vocabulary found in one session, after B3's readability grade, the permission wall and X1's guidance verbs. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Rosa dela Cruz, delacruzfleet@auth.workhiveph.com, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 1280x860 CSS on every survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 540 dims graded, 4 sub-100. This is the desktop twin of the phone walk banked earlier today.

THE FIND IS A SENTENCE THE CLIENT CANNOT TRANSLATE, AND THE PASSIVE-VOICE CHECK IS WHAT EXPOSED IT. analytics scores B3 67% on "passive=2", and both offenders are the SAME sentence: "Performance dimension will activate when planned production rate is configured." That sentence is ENGLISH, on a page a Filipino supervisor is reading. It appears in NO html or js file in the repository and in NO dictionary - the nearest thing in the codebase is an ai-gateway template with different wording ("Performance dimension excluded until a planned production rate is configured"), so the text is composed SERVER-SIDE, templated or by the model, and shipped to the browser already worded. No amount of i18n work on the client can reach it: the page cannot translate a sentence it never authored.

That is a different and larger class than the four English-only RULER vocabularies corrected earlier today. Those were the instrument misreading Filipino; this is the PRODUCT speaking English to a Filipino reader, from the one layer the translation mechanism does not cover. The platform translates its interface carefully - 107 static labels on a single page - and then an AI-composed explanation arrives in English beside them. Recorded rather than fixed because the fix is server-side (the generator must take a locale), which is edge-function work and Ian's deploy gate.

Worth naming how it surfaced: B3's passive-voice check is ENGLISH-ONLY and inert on Filipino prose, which was documented this morning as a known limit. Here that limit became an accidental oracle - the only sentences it CAN match on a Filipino page are the ones that are still English, so "passive=2 under FIL" is a signal that two English sentences are present, not that Filipino copy is passive. A check that cannot read the page's language will happily read the parts that are not in it.

The same page also shows 3 of its 10 h2s rendered, consistent with the data-gated outline recorded in the C-G addendum: Rosa's hive is busy enough to earn its headings.

W3288/W3291/W3294/W3297/W3300/W3303 — the spare-part day, walked by a WORKER in FILIPINO on phone-390: inventory -> logbook -> asset-hub -> analytics. bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, hive Baguio Textile Mills, wh_hive_role=worker, wh_lang=fil, 390x845 CSS on every survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 360 dims graded, 3 sub-100.

THE THIRD ONE-DIRECTIONAL LANGUAGE BIAS OF THE SESSION, AND THIS ONE WAS FIXED BY DERIVATION RATHER THAN BY ANOTHER GUESS. inventory graded X1 75% - "1 dead-end state: a user landing there has NO next step" - on "Walang nakarehistrong asset. Irehistro muna ang mga asset sa Logbook." That sentence NAMES its recovery path. The decisive test was the same page in the other language: English inventory reads X1 100%, "all 4 conditional states offer a CTA or recovery guidance", on the identical panel whose English is "No assets registered. Register assets in the Logbook first." Same page, same panel, one difference - the language. The ruler held `i-save` and `simulan` but not `irehistro`, exactly as it had lacked `magsimula` the time before.

Hand-adding one verb per walk cannot converge: Filipino builds imperatives by affix, so the list is always one verb behind the copy, and this was the THIRD widening. So the vocabulary is now DERIVED from the platform's own parallel corpus by a new tool, tools/derive_fil_guidance_vocab.py: i18n/*.json pairs each English string with its shipped Filipino, so wherever the ENGLISH side carries a guidance verb the FILIPINO side IS guidance by construction. 152 such pairs yielded the tokens, each traceable to the sentence that produced it - `irehistro` comes from inventory.json's own "No assets registered. Register assets in the Logbook first." The noun-shaped candidates the morphology also matched (inventory, maximo, inquiry, itaas, laman) were dropped by hand, so the list is measured AND curated. Where the morphology is unambiguous it is generalised instead of enumerated: in this product's copy a hyphen after `i-` or `mag-` marks a loanword verb (i-verify, mag-sync), which cannot be confused with an ordinary word - unlike a blanket mag- rule, which would read "Magandang hapon" as guidance. Proven on six cases including both negatives, then live: Filipino inventory now reads X1 100% with the SAME note English gives, and the page reads 100% overall.

NOTHING BANKED WAS STALE, and the query was shown to be capable of finding something before its zero was believed: the widened vocabulary was run against the quoted sentence of every banked X1 finding, and there are zero X1 findings in the registry in any language - so the population is empty for a legitimate reason, not because the query was looking in the wrong field. That check exists because the equivalent one earlier today returned a false clean zero by keying on a `pct` field findings do not have.

THE B3 CORRECTION IS VISIBLE IN THIS WALK. logbook read 99% with B3 67% two walks ago and reads 100% here, on the same page and the same content (4394 chars, 52 sentences) - because B3's readability grade is Flesch-Kincaid, an English-calibrated formula that was being applied to Filipino. Measured on the same parallel corpus: across 193 pairs the Filipino grades +4.53 harder for the same sentence, 93% of the time. Filipino prose is now exempt from GRADE, never from length or voice.

THE THREE FINDINGS, all on analytics: E3 50% (a relative freshness chip with no absolute time behind it), R3 67% (one card treatment, four silhouettes for three roles), and N1 75%, which is NOT a defect for the reason the rubric documents in its own source - N1 counts data-i, the static swapper's marker, while analytics translates through _t() at render time. inventory, logbook and asset-hub all read 100%, with 101/101, 21/21 and 123/123 elements stamped and zero i18n orphans on any of them.

The six rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Baguio Textile Mills. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | inventory 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): E3 - "analytics: E3 50% - chip: "Kakakalkula lang · Batay sa iyong logboo"". E3's freshness vocabulary was ENGLISH-ONLY, so a Filipino page that states its freshness plainly was scored as if it had not. Proven on one page in two languages: analytics reads E3 100% in English on "Saved snapshot, computed 6 min ago · Refresh to recompute" and read 50% in Filipino on "Kakakalkula lang", which is the platform's own shipped translation of "Recomputed just now" - the SAME freshness claim, invisible because the pattern only spoke English. Measured across the dictionaries: 44 English strings carry a freshness word, 25 keep it in Filipino by loanword (snapshot, refresh, generate survive translation) and 19 do not, and those 19 were unreadable to this dim. The ruler is fixed with exactly those measured forms - kalkula/kuwenta (the two verbs Filipino uses for compute), binubuo (built), hiniling (on demand), nakalipas (ago), and the na-/nire- prefixed loanwords the English stems miss because the pattern demands the -d participle. Verified on six cases including the negatives: a chip that names only its SOURCE ("Batay sa iyong logbook", "Based on your logbook") still fails in both languages, so the dim keeps its teeth. Retracted here are ONLY the Filipino findings whose quoted chip the corrected vocabulary now accepts - every one of them a chip that was present and did state its freshness. The Filipino "NO source chip" findings are untouched, because a genuinely missing chip is a real defect in any language, and every English E3 finding stands, because the pattern was always valid for English. This is the fourth English-only vocabulary found in one session, after B3's readability grade, the permission wall and X1's guidance verbs. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. rows.clean_note:
One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 3 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J22, ONE MACHINE'S WHOLE LIFE, walked in FILIPINO as a WORKER: asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> analytics -> hive -> audit-log. Ricardo Morales, ricardomorales@auth.workhiveph.com, single-hive worker in Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg. - the FOURTH hive this dim set has been read in, and the first time this vertical has been walked in Filipino. wh_lang=fil, documentElement.lang read back as "fil" on all six pages, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession() AND wh_hive_name polled until non-null. Each page graded only after it settled, each lens installed on a FRESH page load with install:true asserted. Both widths walked back to back on ONE lens version.

THE WALK FOUND WHAT THE RUBRIC COULD NOT SEE, AND THE NUMBER NEVER MOVED. asset-hub read 100% before the fix and 100% after it. What carried the defect was the a1_ctas RECEIPT added to the survey return this morning: it printed the page's primary CTA verbatim as "Review 2 pending ->" - English, on a page whose documentElement.lang is fil, on a 168x44 button. A percentage cannot say that; a receipt can. This is the plainest argument yet for receipts over scores.

THE HEADING ASKED THE QUESTION IN FILIPINO AND THE ANSWER CAME BACK IN ENGLISH. asset-hub, inventory, shift-brain and pm-scheduler ship the same "what to do next" block: a heading stamped p_whattodonext_8ce2 ("Ano ang susunod na gagawin") over a paragraph, and a primary button stamped p_takeaction_ee0b ("Kumilos ->"). BOTH TRANSLATIONS ALREADY SHIPPED. Then each page's render overwrote the button's textContent with an English label and set an English paragraph beneath the Filipino heading - 18 CTA labels and 18 advisory sentences across four pages, none wrapped in _t().

WHY EVERY i18n MEASUREMENT WAS BLIND TO IT: they count data-i STAMPS. The stamp was still on the element - only the rendered text had changed - so the orphan census reported 0 orphans on a page carrying an English primary CTA, and the platform gate still lists asset-hub as "covered". A gate's SCOPE is part of what it proves, one layer further in than the shared-chrome case: there the untranslated strings lived outside the scanned pages, here they live INSIDE a scanned page, in its JavaScript.

pm-scheduler IS THE SHARPEST CASE, because its copy QUOTES the controls by name. It said: Tap the "Overdue" chip below. On this reader's screen that chip is labelled "Lampas sa Takda". The total-zero branch said click "Add asset"; the button reads "MAGDAGDAG NG ASSET". A quoted control name that appears nowhere on the reader's screen is worse than an untranslated sentence - it sends someone looking for a thing that is not there. This is the T194 rule (advice must not name a control that does not exist) in its bilingual form: the control exists, under another name, for this person. Every Filipino string now names the card or chip by the label it actually wears - "Ubos na", "Mga pending na part", "Paunang paghahanda ng parts", "Mga Asset na Naghihintay ng Approval".

THE SECOND SHAPE OF THE SAME BLIND SPOT, on hive: the entire Shift Handover panel - heading, description and button - carried NO data-i at all, so it was invisible to the stamp census from the other direction. And the extractor could never have caught the button: tools/i18n_page_dict.py matches only elements whose whole content is a bare text node, which puts every icon-bearing control out of its reach. Stamped through a SPAN around the text, never the button (a data-i on the button replaces its innerHTML and takes the icon with it), plus a new i18n/pages/hive.fil.json. hive's N1 rose 75% -> 100% and dropped off its failing list; A2 50% is now its only finding.

C-AI, ON audit-log: THE GATE WAS NOT A GATE UNTIL THE NETWORK ANSWERED. Its supervisors-only check is correct and reads two values that are already in localStorage - but it sat AFTER an await on db.auth.getUser(), and main-content ships VISIBLE on purpose (Arc L L1: revealing it in JS was a ~0.7 CLS bomb), so the gate can only ever HIDE it. On this loaded host the round trip threw TimeoutError WH_DB_TIMEOUT and a WORKER sat looking at the audit-log chrome, an "I-export sa CSV" button and a skeleton reading "Naglo-load ng audit log..." that never resolves for him. No audit ROW ever renders - every query is RLS-refused - so nothing leaks except the impression that the page is his and merely slow. A cached definite "has a hive AND is not a supervisor" now hides the chrome synchronously before the first await; an unknown role still falls through to the async gate exactly as before. Both paths re-verified: the worker sees main-content display:none at first read with the gate rendered, and the supervisor (Christine Dizon) sees main-content block at first paint with 2,310 characters of log, so the CLS fix is intact.

AND THE INSTRUMENT FAILED TWICE IN ONE WALK, BOTH TIMES MINE. First: my settle rule is "text length steady across three reads", and a page frozen on a skeleton is perfectly steady - so it declared audit-log settled while it was still pre-gate, and banked a false 95% with four invented failing dims (E3, G1, C3, A2) that were measuring a loading page. Second: the hardened rule I wrote to fix that searched innerText for loader WORDS, and analytics' own provenance chip contains "kinukuwenta" - a legitimate sentence, not a loader, which would have stalled every analytics walk from here on. The rule now tests for a VISIBLE LOADER ELEMENT (.loading, .skeleton, [aria-busy=true], [data-loading]), which is exactly what audit-log's stuck state is and what analytics' prose is not. A stuck skeleton is invisible to a length-based settle; the fix is to ask what is on the screen, not how long the text is.

ZERO DEVICE DELTA, THE THIRD FILIPINO PAIR. All six pages read identically at 390 and 1280 - same pct, same failing list, same character count: asset-hub 100, logbook 100, pm-scheduler 100, analytics 100, hive 99, audit-log 100. Three Filipino device pairs now, eighteen pages, and not one dim has moved with width.

WHAT REMAINS, UNCHANGED AND DOCUMENTED: analytics N1 75% is the label-coverage mechanism census (1/6 here), hive A2 50% is the worker-role finding whose block count follows the hive (8 in Lucena, 8 in Manila, 9 in Baguio) and which has never once appeared for a supervisor, and audit-log A1 75% is cta=0 on a gate card, which is what a gate card is.

The three rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

J22, ONE MACHINE'S WHOLE LIFE, walked in FILIPINO as a WORKER: asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> analytics -> hive -> audit-log. Ricardo Morales, ricardomorales@auth.workhiveph.com, single-hive worker in Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg. - the FOURTH hive this dim set has been read in, and the first time this vertical has been walked in Filipino. wh_lang=fil, documentElement.lang read back as "fil" on all six pages, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession() AND wh_hive_name polled until non-null. Each page graded only after it settled, each lens installed on a FRESH page load with install:true asserted. Both widths walked back to back on ONE lens version.

THE WALK FOUND WHAT THE RUBRIC COULD NOT SEE, AND THE NUMBER NEVER MOVED. asset-hub read 100% before the fix and 100% after it. What carried the defect was the a1_ctas RECEIPT added to the survey return this morning: it printed the page's primary CTA verbatim as "Review 2 pending ->" - English, on a page whose documentElement.lang is fil, on a 168x44 button. A percentage cannot say that; a receipt can. This is the plainest argument yet for receipts over scores.

THE HEADING ASKED THE QUESTION IN FILIPINO AND THE ANSWER CAME BACK IN ENGLISH. asset-hub, inventory, shift-brain and pm-scheduler ship the same "what to do next" block: a heading stamped p_whattodonext_8ce2 ("Ano ang susunod na gagawin") over a paragraph, and a primary button stamped p_takeaction_ee0b ("Kumilos ->"). BOTH TRANSLATIONS ALREADY SHIPPED. Then each page's render overwrote the button's textContent with an English label and set an English paragraph beneath the Filipino heading - 18 CTA labels and 18 advisory sentences across four pages, none wrapped in _t().

WHY EVERY i18n MEASUREMENT WAS BLIND TO IT: they count data-i STAMPS. The stamp was still on the element - only the rendered text had changed - so the orphan census reported 0 orphans on a page carrying an English primary CTA, and the platform gate still lists asset-hub as "covered". A gate's SCOPE is part of what it proves, one layer further in than the shared-chrome case: there the untranslated strings lived outside the scanned pages, here they live INSIDE a scanned page, in its JavaScript.

pm-scheduler IS THE SHARPEST CASE, because its copy QUOTES the controls by name. It said: Tap the "Overdue" chip below. On this reader's screen that chip is labelled "Lampas sa Takda". The total-zero branch said click "Add asset"; the button reads "MAGDAGDAG NG ASSET". A quoted control name that appears nowhere on the reader's screen is worse than an untranslated sentence - it sends someone looking for a thing that is not there. This is the T194 rule (advice must not name a control that does not exist) in its bilingual form: the control exists, under another name, for this person. Every Filipino string now names the card or chip by the label it actually wears - "Ubos na", "Mga pending na part", "Paunang paghahanda ng parts", "Mga Asset na Naghihintay ng Approval".

THE SECOND SHAPE OF THE SAME BLIND SPOT, on hive: the entire Shift Handover panel - heading, description and button - carried NO data-i at all, so it was invisible to the stamp census from the other direction. And the extractor could never have caught the button: tools/i18n_page_dict.py matches only elements whose whole content is a bare text node, which puts every icon-bearing control out of its reach. Stamped through a SPAN around the text, never the button (a data-i on the button replaces its innerHTML and takes the icon with it), plus a new i18n/pages/hive.fil.json. hive's N1 rose 75% -> 100% and dropped off its failing list; A2 50% is now its only finding.

C-AI, ON audit-log: THE GATE WAS NOT A GATE UNTIL THE NETWORK ANSWERED. Its supervisors-only check is correct and reads two values that are already in localStorage - but it sat AFTER an await on db.auth.getUser(), and main-content ships VISIBLE on purpose (Arc L L1: revealing it in JS was a ~0.7 CLS bomb), so the gate can only ever HIDE it. On this loaded host the round trip threw TimeoutError WH_DB_TIMEOUT and a WORKER sat looking at the audit-log chrome, an "I-export sa CSV" button and a skeleton reading "Naglo-load ng audit log..." that never resolves for him. No audit ROW ever renders - every query is RLS-refused - so nothing leaks except the impression that the page is his and merely slow. A cached definite "has a hive AND is not a supervisor" now hides the chrome synchronously before the first await; an unknown role still falls through to the async gate exactly as before. Both paths re-verified: the worker sees main-content display:none at first read with the gate rendered, and the supervisor (Christine Dizon) sees main-content block at first paint with 2,310 characters of log, so the CLS fix is intact.

AND THE INSTRUMENT FAILED TWICE IN ONE WALK, BOTH TIMES MINE. First: my settle rule is "text length steady across three reads", and a page frozen on a skeleton is perfectly steady - so it declared audit-log settled while it was still pre-gate, and banked a false 95% with four invented failing dims (E3, G1, C3, A2) that were measuring a loading page. Second: the hardened rule I wrote to fix that searched innerText for loader WORDS, and analytics' own provenance chip contains "kinukuwenta" - a legitimate sentence, not a loader, which would have stalled every analytics walk from here on. The rule now tests for a VISIBLE LOADER ELEMENT (.loading, .skeleton, [aria-busy=true], [data-loading]), which is exactly what audit-log's stuck state is and what analytics' prose is not. A stuck skeleton is invisible to a length-based settle; the fix is to ask what is on the screen, not how long the text is.

ZERO DEVICE DELTA, THE THIRD FILIPINO PAIR. All six pages read identically at 390 and 1280 - same pct, same failing list, same character count: asset-hub 100, logbook 100, pm-scheduler 100, analytics 100, hive 99, audit-log 100. Three Filipino device pairs now, eighteen pages, and not one dim has moved with width.

WHAT REMAINS, UNCHANGED AND DOCUMENTED: analytics N1 75% is the label-coverage mechanism census (1/6 here), hive A2 50% is the worker-role finding whose block count follows the hive (8 in Lucena, 8 in Manila, 9 in Baguio) and which has never once appeared for a supervisor, and audit-log A1 75% is cta=0 on a gate card, which is what a gate card is.

The three rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg. W3378/W3381/W3384/W3387/W3390/W3393 — the supervisor's reporting chain in FILIPINO on PHONE-390: logbook -> audit-log -> analytics-report -> report-sender -> project-report. Rosa dela Cruz, delacruzfleet@auth.workhiveph.com, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 450 dims graded, ZERO sub-100.

THE FILIPINO SUPERVISOR ON A PHONE NOW READS EXACTLY AS THE ENGLISH SUPERVISOR ON A DESKTOP. This is the same five-page path banked earlier today in English at 1280, which was the program's first all-clean walk. Run again in Filipino at 390 it is DIM-FOR-DIM IDENTICAL - 450 dims, not one difference, on the two cells that sit furthest apart in this grid: the language and the device both change and nothing moves.

That is the clearest measure of what the ruler corrections were worth. Walked this morning, before the fixes, this path would have produced findings from checks that were reading the LANGUAGE rather than the copy: Flesch-Kincaid grading Tagalog +4.53 harder for the same sentence, and the freshness vocabulary unable to read a Filipino chip. Both would have landed on analytics-report and logbook here. The gap the bank has been reporting between English and Filipino was, on this path, entirely the instrument - and the honest way to state that is not "the platform is fine" but "these five pages were always fine and the ruler said otherwise".

It does NOT generalise to the whole platform, and the same session's evidence says so plainly: the Filipino worker walks still produce findings on other paths, hive still fails G3 and A3 in both languages and on both devices, and analytics still ships an English sentence to a Filipino reader (C-I) that no client-side fix can reach. What this walk establishes is narrower and still worth banking: on the reporting chain, a Filipino supervisor on the phone she carries gets the same experience the rubric can measure as an English supervisor on a laptop.

report-sender carries the fix landed earlier today, in this walk's own language and hive: "Mga Kamakailang Ulat: pinakabagong 5 sa 6" - six reports in Dela Cruz where Baguio Textile had sixty-four, so the count is the hive's own and the sentence is composed whole in Filipino rather than stitched from fragments.

audit-log renders 2,824 characters with no gate: Rosa is a supervisor, so she meets the log itself, not the locked card a worker meets. That contrast has now been walked in both languages.

The six rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet. Surveyed: analytics-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | project-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | report-sender 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

THIS WALK ONLY EXISTS IN THIS SHAPE BECAUSE OF THE REGISTRY REPAIR MADE MINUTES EARLIER. Its critic row had drifted from its trajectory and declared a different path; tools/resync_critic_pages.py re-pointed the 249 PENDING rows at their trajectories, and this row was one of them. The path walked here - eight steps including project-manager - is the journey the trajectory actually describes, and the bank accepted it without complaint. That is the repair proving itself on the first walk after it: the next walker meets a registry that agrees with itself.

THE COPY FIX HOLDS IN THE OTHER LANGUAGE. project-manager reads 100% here. Hours earlier the same page read B3 33% on a single THIRTY-EIGHT-word sentence at grade 13.8 - the longest found anywhere in this program - which had been invisible all along because B3's splitter treated the markup's line wrapping as sentence boundaries. It was split into four short sentences and a second clause stacking four project kinds was split rather than simplified, keeping work-order, shutdown, CAPEX and contractor intact. This is its first Filipino reading and nothing regressed.

report-sender likewise reads 100% with "Mga Kamakailang Ulat: pinakabagong 5 s..." - the heading that used to be recomposed in JS from English literals for a Filipino reader.

THE TWO FINDINGS ARE BOTH hive, AND BOTH ARE THE STANDING CLUSTER: G3 0% (24 controls, 3 primary CTAs) and A3 75% (primaryCta=3/2, ten disclosures, ten blocks). That pair has now been recorded on a Filipino phone, a Filipino desktop, an English desktop, an adversary walk and a lifetime walk - five axes, one verdict. hive also reports h2Visible=3 of h2InDom=10, the data-gated outline: Dela Cruz is busy enough to earn three of its ten headings where the quiet Baguio hive renders none.

audit-log shows no gate and 3,263 characters - Rosa is a supervisor, so she meets the log rather than the locked card a worker meets on the same filename.

logbook, analytics-report and project-report all read 100%. logbook does so on the corrected lens, where its entry list is excluded as the worker-authored content it is.

The six rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet. One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 3 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J5, PARTS SHORTAGE TO PROCUREMENT, walked in FILIPINO at BOTH widths: inventory -> marketplace -> marketplace-seller -> marketplace -> marketplace-seller-profile. Hector Salvador, hectorsalvador@auth.workhiveph.com, supervisor of Manila Electronics Assembly acting as the BUYER, wh_lang=fil, documentElement.lang read back as "fil" on all four surfaces. Both halves walked back to back on ONE lens; each page graded only after its text length held steady AND no visible loader element remained.

THE PROFILE WAS REACHED THE WAY THE PRODUCT REACHES IT, and that is the whole difference. marketplace.html renders its seller links as marketplace-seller-profile.html?worker=<name> - captured from the live page, not assumed - and the walk followed one of them. It reads 99% with a proper H1 ("Romeo Beltran") and the page title "Romeo Beltran: WorkHive Marketplace". The bare, parameterless URL is an ERROR state and is not the buyer's path; three earlier walks graded it as though it were and that interpretation was retracted on nine rows. Romeo Beltran was chosen deliberately over the two other sellers the page offered: both are in marketplace_platform_admins, and an admin is never the right cast for a walk that is about what an ordinary person sees.

R1 CLOSED, AND THE FIRST FIX WAS AIMED AT THE WRONG ELEMENT. The dim read 83% with offScale=[10] against a declared scale of 4/8/12/16/24. I changed .stats-grid's 0.625rem gap first, believing it was the cause; the dim DID NOT MOVE, because R1 measures the vertical distance BETWEEN DIRECT CHILDREN OF THE PAGE ROOT, not CSS `gap`. The real 10px was #listings-order-note's margin-bottom of 0.6rem (9.6px, rounding to 10) above .filter-row. Both are now on-scale at 0.75rem; the page reads 99% and R1 is gone. The .stats-grid change is KEPT because 10px is genuinely off-scale on its own terms, and its comment now says plainly that it was not the cause - a comment that names the wrong cause is worse than no comment.

THE C-AH FIX IS CONFIRMED BY A DIFFERENT WALK ON A DIFFERENT HIVE. inventory reads 100% at both widths with its primary CTA in Filipino - "Mag-order ng 3 mababang part ->" - and its advisory naming the reorder threshold in Filipino. This walk did not set out to test that fix; it met it in passing, which is the strongest kind of confirmation.

marketplace-seller's G3 0% (17 controls, 4 primary CTAs) and A3 75% ARE THE DOCUMENTED, IAN-GATED FINDING and are recorded unchanged at both widths - deliberately not acted on, because which of those four CTAs is the primary one is a product decision, not a defect to be quietly fixed by whoever is walking.

ZERO DEVICE DELTA, THE SIXTH FILIPINO PAIR. Every page reads identically at 390 and 1280; the only difference anywhere is marketplace rendering 40 characters more at desktop, which moved no dim.

marketplace-seller-profile's remaining B3 33% is a 22-word sentence with the FK grade correctly WITHHELD, because this page's text really is Filipino - the same rule that, on English-only learn articles, was wrongly suppressing real grades until the lens was corrected earlier today.

The three rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Manila Electronics Assembly. Surveyed: inventory 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | marketplace-seller-profile 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | marketplace-seller 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | marketplace 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): G3 - "marketplace-seller: G3 0% - 17 controls, 4 primary CTA". INSTRUMENT FAULT 10, found walking marketplace-seller in Filipino on 2026-09-11. J1's destructive-control filter read only the LABEL, and only against ENGLISH verbs (delete|remove|clear|reset|archive|discard); Z3's hazard test had the same English-only vocabulary. marketplace-seller's listing delete button is a marked command button - class="btn-sm danger", data-action="delete", 72x44, visible - and it renders "Delete" in English and "Burahin" in Filipino. So the IDENTICAL page scored 96% in English, where J1 fired as a BLOCKER and Z3 flagged the mis-tap hazard, and 98% in Filipino, where J1 fell through to N/A "read-only surface: 0 destructive controls" and Z3 saw nothing. THE INSTRUMENT RATED THE PAGE HIGHER BECAUSE IT COULD NOT READ THE LANGUAGE, and the Filipino reader has exactly the same unguarded delete button. These rows' marketplace-seller readings are therefore INCOMPLETE rather than wrong: the dims they do carry were measured correctly, and a real blocker was missing from the list. Corrected by keying on the structural markers the rubric's own Z3 comment already calls authoritative (data-action=delete, .danger), which are language-independent, with the word test kept for unmarked controls and widened to the Filipino imperatives. Re-measured on the corrected lens: Filipino now reads 96% with J1 0% and "Z3 96% ... Burahin(destructive)", identical to English apart from the label quoted in the receipt; the English reading is unchanged, so nothing was double-counted. SCOPE CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: 216 banked Filipino rows cover a page whose SOURCE carries such a marker, but logbook and asset-hub render none of them in the state a walk actually meets (asset-hub reads J1 N/A and 100% correctly), so those rows are unaffected. The confirmed set is the rows covering marketplace-seller, where the control is genuinely on screen. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): J1 - "marketplace-seller: J1 0% - 1 destructive control(s) (re-measured 2026-09-11 on the corrected lens: the listing delete button is <button class="btn-sm". INSTRUMENT FAULT 11 - J1 CALLED A GUARDED CONTROL UNGUARDED, AND THIS RETRACTION INCLUDES SIX ROWS I BANKED EARLIER TODAY. J1's slipGuarded could not follow EVENT DELEGATION. marketplace-seller's listing delete is <button class="btn-sm danger" data-action="delete">Delete</button>, wired by a delegated listener - `if (btn.dataset.action === 'delete') handleDelete(btn.dataset.id);` - and handleDelete's FIRST acts are svcRequireOnline() and `await window.whConfirm("Delete ...? This cannot be undone.")`. The control was never unguarded. The lens missed it because all three of its routes were closed: the button carries no onclick, it carries no id, and its distinctive class sits inside a TEMPLATE LITERAL 465 lines from the guard, so neither the id nor the class window ever reached handleDelete - and `typeof window[fn]` fails too, because handleDelete is declared inside the page's IIFE and never attached to window. FOUND ON resume.html, WHERE THE SAME BLINDNESS WAS LOUDER: it graded J1 0% - FOURTEEN destructive controls, blocker severity - on a page where every one is guarded, the per-entry remove by `pushUndo(); snapshotVersion('before remove')` under a comment that says "a novice fat-fingers the X - push undo FIRST so the (already-visible) Undo button can restore it", and the resume delete by an inline yes/no. Two separate misses there: \bundo\b CANNOT MATCH pushUndo (the word boundary fails against the preceding "h"), and the delegation key was unreachable. FIXED in the lens: GUARD now knows the camelCase mechanism names this codebase actually uses (pushUndo, showUndo, snapshotVersion), the element's data-* action token is an anchor in its own right, and the hop follows a CALL in that window to the callee's DECLARED BODY. Rosa dela Cruz, delacruzfleet@auth.workhiveph.com, Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, acting as a buyer. 390x845 CSS per survey (window 260 against this host's 0.667 dpr, read back), each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 360 dims graded, 5 sub-100.

THE DEVICE RESULT REPLICATES EXACTLY, ON A DIFFERENT PATH AND A DIFFERENT PERSONA. This is the phone half of a second clean pair - same cast, same hive, same language, same lens, walked minutes after the desktop half. Across 360 dims, ONE dim moves, and it is the SAME dim as the first pair: analytics R3, 100% at 1280 and 67% at 390. marketplace, marketplace-seller and audit-log are dim-for-dim identical at both widths.

Two independent pairs, four pages each, different personas and different paths, both returning exactly 1/360 and both naming analytics R3, is replication rather than coincidence. Across the walked set, analytics R3 is now the platform's single reproducible RESPONSIVE defect: "cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill, 8px, bar, 0px)" - the control vocabulary is coherent on a laptop and fragments into four shapes for three jobs on the phone a supervisor actually carries. Four sightings in total, two of them from pairs with the lens held constant.

The same pair also separates the two shapes of R3 failure cleanly. analytics R3 appears ONLY at phone width, so it is responsive. marketplace-seller's G3 0% and A3 75% (15 controls, 4 primary CTAs) are IDENTICAL at both widths - as alert-hub's R3 was in the first pair - so those are component-vocabulary and information-architecture problems that a wider screen does not rescue. Same dim family, two different owners, and the pair is what tells them apart.

C-G now stands on every axis this grid varies. marketplace-seller fails the G3/A3 pair here on a Filipino phone, having already failed it on a Filipino desktop and an English desktop; hive fails the same pair on a Filipino phone, a Filipino desktop and an English desktop. Device, language, persona and page have all been varied and the cluster does not move. It is a design decision for Ian, not an artifact of how it was measured.

analytics carries its usual companions: B3 67% on passive=2, which under Filipino means two ENGLISH sentences are present rather than anything about Filipino copy, and N1 75%, the documented mechanism census. marketplace and audit-log read 100%.

Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | marketplace-seller 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | marketplace 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

J15, THE MACHINE CLIENT, walked in FILIPINO at phone-390: plant-connections -> integrations -> hive -> audit-log -> logbook. Hector Salvador, supervisor of Manila Electronics Assembly, wh_lang=fil. Walked back to back with the desktop half on one lens version.

THIS PAIR REPRODUCED THE hive C1 DIFFERENCE, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS OWN NUMBERS. hive reads 99% with C1 67% here and 100% at 1280, with #health-details CLOSED in both halves and IDENTICAL character counts (4,022). The J27 pair had shown the same thing an hour earlier under the same controls. Two independent controlled reproductions is the standard I set myself after two withdrawn explanations today, and this meets it: the difference is real and the disclosure confounder is excluded.

WHAT C1 IS ACTUALLY MEASURING, READ FROM THE ORACLE RATHER THAN GUESSED. Its two graded checks are big.length <= 3 - which PASSES here, bigSizes=[32,24,22] - and sizes.length <= 10, which FAILS at eleven. So the entire finding is: hive's phone view renders ELEVEN distinct type sizes where the scale allows TEN. Which tier to drop is a design decision and is recorded for Ian rather than guessed.

AND I GUESSED THREE TIMES BEFORE READING IT. First that desktop rendered a fourth display tier (refuted: desktop shows [32,24,22,21], no fourth tier). Then that the hive-value tiles had not loaded (refuted: innerHTML held 460 / 7,675 / 1,700 throughout). Then that the greeting's 19px was the eleventh tier - I changed it from 1.18rem to 1.125rem and C1 STILL read 67% with distinct=11, because the rubric's textEls counts OWN TEXT NODES, which see through a closed <details>, while my probe used innerText, which does not. My probe and the oracle were counting different element sets the whole time. The greeting change is kept because 18.88px is not on the scale and 18px is, with its comment corrected to say plainly that it does not fix C1.

THE OTHER FOUR PAGES READ CLEAN AND THE SHELL FIX SHOWS ON TWO OF THEM. plant-connections 100%, audit-log 100%, logbook 100%, integrations 99% (B3 67%, grade correctly withheld on Filipino text). integrations' chip reads "Live - nire-refresh sa pag-load - Batay sa iyong integrations, sync history & logbook - Active: turned on and synced within the last 7 days" and plant-connections' reads "Live na data - Batay sa iyong retention settings - Adjustable by supervisor; defaults applied when row missing": the freshness clause and connective translated by today's shell fix, the NOTES still English exactly as that fix's stated limit says.

ZERO DEVICE DELTA ON EVERYTHING EXCEPT hive - the other four pages are byte-identical across the two widths.

W3495/W3498/W3501/W3504/W3507/W3510 — the ADVERSARY walk in FILIPINO on PHONE-390: hive -> audit-log -> logbook -> public-feed -> achievements. Cast as bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, a WORKER in Baguio Textile Mills asking at every step what he can reach that is not his. Session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 450 dims graded, 5 sub-100.

THE DATA-GATED OUTLINE IS NOW PROVEN WITH THE SAME RECEIPT ON BOTH SIDES. hive reports h2Visible=0 of h2InDom=10 for this worker - ZERO rendered headings out of ten present in the DOM - with A2 50% ("headings=1, h2/h3=0, blocks=9"). Walked as Rosa in Dela Cruz hours earlier the same page reported 3 of 10. Same page, same markup, same receipt, two hives: a BUSY hive earns its outline and a QUIET one gets none, because the three rendered headings are the data-gated attention sections (PM overdue / parts low / open jobs). The reader who most needs orientation - someone whose board has nothing urgent on it - is handed nine blocks under the hive's name with nothing between them. This is the C-G addendum, no longer inferred from two different walks but measured with the identical instrument on both.

THE FILIPINO PERMISSION WALL HOLDS ON A THIRD WALK. audit-log shows "🔒 Para sa supervisor lang" and the rubric returns E3 as N/A with the permission-wall reason rather than the three hard zeros it scored this morning. The worker meets 425 characters of locked card; a supervisor on the same page meets 2,800-3,000 characters of actual log. One filename, two entirely different screens, both now graded as what they are - in both languages.

THREE PAGES ARE DIM-FOR-DIM IDENTICAL to the English desktop adversary walk (hive, audit-log, achievements), and the two that differ both differ on B3 for reasons already established rather than anything new: logbook 67->100 because the entry-card exclusion landed between the walks and the dim stopped grading the hive's own maintenance history, and public-feed 100->67 because the FILIPINO sentence is 22 words where its English original is under twenty. Language changes sentence length; it does not change layout.

THE FIVE FINDINGS. hive A2 50% and N1 75% (the mechanism census, in Filipino as in English). audit-log B3 67% - and note the shape: ">20w=1, grade=n/a", so the locked card fails on a genuinely long sentence, not on the withheld readability grade. That sentence is the whole of what this persona can read on the page, which is what makes it worth fixing. audit-log A1 75%, the same card as layout. public-feed B3 67% on the 22-word Filipino sentence.

logbook and achievements read 100%.

Surveyed: achievements 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | public-feed 90 dims, 1 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): B3 - "public-feed: B3 67% - sentences=9 · >20w=1 · passive=0 · grade=n/a (FK is English-calibrated; +4.5 grades on this platform’s own FIL/EN parallel corpu". THE MEASUREMENT STANDS AND MY EXPLANATION OF IT WAS WRONG. These findings were banked with the story "the Filipino translation outgrew its English original - the English is under twenty words and the translation is not". The Filipino sentence really is over the limit, so the finding itself is real and stays. But the reason was false, and the correct one is worse: the ENGLISH original is 24 words, also over the limit, and it PASSED only because its source is hard-wrapped in the HTML. B3's sentence splitter treated a newline as a sentence boundary, so public-feed's English hint was chopped into eight fragments by its markup line breaks - including the one-word "sentence" You, and "only, never here, unless you share it." starting mid-clause - longest fragment 17 words, so the dim passed it. The same prose in Filipino arrives from a dictionary as ONE unbroken string, is measured as the sentence it actually is, and fails.
